elements.evidence: Article XII-A requires Licensor to indemnify Licensee for IP claims but does not require Licensor to defend Licensee.

elements.evidence: Article XII-A requires Licensor to indemnify Licensee against third-party claims alleging that the Licensed Technology infringes or misappropriates an intellectual property right.

elements.evidence: Article XII-A contains no defense obligation and names only Licensee as the protected party.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnification obligations must extend to Customer's affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.

elements.evidence: Article XII-A is limited to IP infringement and misappropriation claims and does not cover Licensor's breach of law.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no Licensor defense obligation or data-breach indemnity.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A does not include data breaches caused by Licensor as an indemnified trigger.

elements.evidence: Article XII-A does not cover claims arising from Licensor's gross negligence.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: No Licensor defense obligation or wilful-misconduct trigger is stated.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A does not cover claims arising from Licensor's wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require notice of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: No notice procedure appears in Article XII-A.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must allocate control of the defense and settlement.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A does not address control of defense or settlement.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require reasonable cooperation by the indemnified party.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A contains no cooperation requirement.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must be limited exclusively to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Article XII retains a substantially broader Licensee indemnity covering exercise of licensed rights, conduct of Licensee's business, and breach of any representation, warranty, obligation, restriction, term, or covenant.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A requires Licensor to indemnify Licensee against third-party claims alleging that the Licensed Technology infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims arising from Customer modifications.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims arising from combinations with items not supplied by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A excludes claims arising from combination of the Licensed Technology with items not supplied by Licensor.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims arising from Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A expressly excludes claims arising from Licensee's specifications.

elements.element: Vendor must have an infringement remedy to procure Customer's right to continue using the affected services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A requires Licensor to procure for Licensee the right to continue using the affected Licensed Technology.

elements.element: Vendor must have an infringement remedy to modify the affected services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A expressly requires Licensor, as an alternative remedy, to modify the affected Licensed Technology.

elements.element: Vendor must have an infringement remedy to replace the affected services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A expressly requires Licensor, as an alternative remedy, to replace the affected Licensed Technology.

elements.element: If procurement, modification, and replacement are unavailable, Vendor must refund the fees paid for the affected services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A requires a refund of fees paid for the affected Licensed Technology if none of the preceding remedies is available.

elements.element: Vendor's aggregate liability for the IP indemnity must be subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A caps Licensor's aggregate liability under that article at three times annual fees paid under the Agreement, and Article XIII(b) expressly excludes those obligations from the lower general cap.

result.reason: The redline satisfies every fallback requirement by adding a Licensor IP indemnity, the three specified exclusions, the procure/modify/replace/refund remedy sequence, and a 3× annual-fees super-cap. It does not satisfy the preferred position because it omits defense, affiliate protection, non-IP Vendor triggers, indemnification procedures, and narrowing of Licensee's existing broad indemnity. The changes are confined to the fallback indemnity and necessary liability carve-outs, preserving unrelated terms. Drafting quality is reduced by the awkward placement of the Article XIII(a) exception in an existing run-on sentence and the undefined measurement period for 'annual fees.'
